title_en: Wang Guangzhi v. Cuqiao Branch of Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. and He Fang — dispute over enforcement objection by a non-party
ruling_gist_en: In cases involving an action for enforcement objection by an outsider, the determination of whether the civil rights and interests claimed by the outsider in respect of the subject matter of enforcement are sufficient to exclude compulsory enforcement shall be made on the basis of the provisions of relevant laws and judicial interpretations regarding civil rights and interests, after ascertaining the substantive law nature and effect of the civil rights and interests of the relevant parties in relation to the subject matter of enforcement. This shall be done by exploring and analyzing the hierarchical relationships among relevant legal norms, the value judgments underlying them, and the legislative purposes, and by taking into consideration, in conjunction with the specific circumstances of different cases, factors such as the professional identity and characteristics of the relevant parties, the degree of fault with respect to the defective status of the rights in the subject matter of enforcement, the status of rights exercise related to transactions involving the subject matter of enforcement, the performance of transactions, and further analyzing the impact of the subject matter of enforcement on the basic living security and pursuit of order by the relevant parties, and making a comprehensive determination.
keywords_en: Civil law; Action for enforcement objection; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Sichuan Province; Natural person; Legal person; Civil Procedure Law; Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Enforcement Objections and Reconsideration Cases by People's Courts; Review standard for outsider's action for enforcement objection; Relationship between expected property right and compulsory enforcement; Determination of civil rights and interests excluding enforcement; Uphold the original judgment; Enforcement objection; Dispute over house ownership; Welfare housing under labor contract; Mortgage loan; Good faith; Dispute over outsider's action for enforcement objection
full_text_en:
Wang Guangzhi v. Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Cuqiao Sub-branch and He Fang — dispute over third-party objection to enforcement

Ruling Summary

In a lawsuit of third-party objection to enforcement, to determine whether the civil rights and interests claimed by the third party with respect to the subject matter of enforcement are sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement, it is necessary to first ascertain the nature and effect of the substantive law with respect to the civil rights and interests of the relevant parties in the subject matter of enforcement in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and judicial interpretations on civil rights and interests. Then, by exploring and analyzing the hierarchical relationship between the relevant legal norms, the value judgments underlying them, and the legislative purposes, and by taking into account specific circumstances such as the professional identity and characteristics of the relevant parties, their degree of fault regarding the defective status of the rights in the subject matter of enforcement, the state of exercise of rights related to transactions in the subject matter of enforcement, the performance status of transactions, and further analyzing the impact of the subject matter of enforcement on the basic living security and the pursuit of order of the relevant parties, a comprehensive determination shall be made.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2019) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 370

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Wang Guangzhi, male, born November 7, 1979, Han Chinese, residing at Lizhou Town, Xichang City, Sichuan Province.

Agent ad litem: Chen Weixiang, lawyer of Sichuan Henghexin Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Miaoyi, lawyer of Sichuan Henghexin Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Cuqiao Sub-branch, domiciled at Section 2, Fujin Road, Cuqiao Town, Wuhou District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

Person in charge: Tang Xiaotang, President of the Sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Liao Xiaoli, lawyer of Sichuan Junhe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ning Xueying, lawyer of Sichuan Junhe Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): He Fang, female, born October 11, 1971, Han Chinese, residing at Qingyang District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province.

In the case of Wang Guangzhi's appeal against the civil judgment of the Sichuan High People's Court (2018) Sichuan Civil First Instance No. 112 concerning a dispute with Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd. Cuqiao Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch) and He Fang over a third-party objection to execution, Wang Guangzhi appealed to this Court. This Court, after filing the case on March 14, 2019, formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law and conducted a trial. Wang Guangzhi and his agents ad litem Chen Weixiang and Wang Miaoyi, the agent ad litem of Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch Liao Xiaoli, and He Fang appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

Wang Guangzhi's appellate requests: 1. Set aside the first-instance judgment; 2. Amend the judgment to confirm that Property A at Jiahong Road, Jinjiang District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province belongs to Wang Guangzhi; 3. Amend the judgment to order He Fang to assist Wang Guangzhi in completing the procedures for the change of ownership registration of the property; 4. Amend the judgment to order a stay of execution on Property A at Jiahong Road, Jinjiang District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, and to lift the seizure measures; 5. The litigation costs of the first and second instances shall be borne jointly by Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch and He Fang. Facts and reasons: 1. Wang Guangzhi has a right of expectation of property ownership over the property in dispute. First, although no strict real estate sale relationship was formed between Wang Guangzhi and He Fang, Wang Guangzhi did enter into a labor contract with the San Yang Kai Tai Apparel Chain Xiangtan Store (hereinafter referred to as the Apparel Store) actually operated by He Fang and Chen Feiping. The Apparel Store voluntarily and for consideration purchased the property in dispute and provided it to Wang Guangzhi as a welfare benefit. Based on the relevant contractual agreements, Wang Guangzhi acquired a right of expectation of property ownership over the property in dispute. Second, the agreements on the payment of the purchase price and bank mortgage installments for the property in dispute in the "Supplementary Agreement to the Labor Contract" and the "Explanation" signed between Wang Guangzhi and the Apparel Store had been modified in the course of actual performance. The property was actually purchased by Wang Guangzhi; the Apparel Store only paid a very small portion of the down payment, with the majority of the down payment paid by Wang Guangzhi. Third, in the "Commercial Housing Subscription Agreement" signed with Sichuan Nanxin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Nanxin Company) on June 13, 2009, the purchasers were listed as Wang Guangzhi and He Fang, indicating that the property was purchased by Wang Guangzhi, but was temporarily registered in He Fang's name as agreed in the labor contract, and was not actually purchased by He Fang. 2. Wang Guangzhi was not at fault for the failure to transfer and register the property in dispute under his name. After the Apparel Store was dissolved, Wang Guangzhi repeatedly communicated with He Fang regarding the property transfer. He Fang and others also acknowledged that Wang Guangzhi had performed his obligations under the labor contract. However, because the bank mortgage loan on the property in dispute had not yet been fully repaid at that time, and the agreed ten-year service period had not yet expired, the transfer registration was not completed in 2014. Later, for his daughter's schooling, Wang Guangzhi sought to complete the transfer in advance. On July 31, 2017, he repaid the remaining mortgage balance of RMB 246,161.83 in full. However, before the property could be transferred to Wang Guangzhi, it was sealed up by the court. Therefore, the first-instance court's finding that Wang Guangzhi did not negotiate with He Fang regarding the ownership and transfer of the property in dispute after the Apparel Store was dissolved in 2014 constitutes a factual error. In summary, Wang Guangzhi enjoys civil rights and interests sufficient to preclude the court's preservation seizure.

Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch argued in defense: 1. No "Sales Contract" or any legal relationship capable of effecting a change in property rights was entered into between Wang Guangzhi and He Fang with respect to the property in dispute. The owner of the property in dispute is He Fang; the Apparel Store does not own the property. The labor contract, supplementary agreement, etc., signed between the Apparel Store and Wang Guangzhi merely established a labor relationship between Wang Guangzhi and the Apparel Store, and the rights and obligations thereunder cannot extend to He Fang or the property in dispute held in He Fang's name. 2. The purchase price for the property was not paid in full by Wang Guangzhi. If the amount paid by Wang Guangzhi exceeded the scope he should have borne under the agreement, he has a right of claim against the Apparel Store. The property transfer registration was not completed because Wang Guangzhi failed to fulfill the full service period stipulated in the labor contract. He does not have a stable right of expectation of property ownership over the property and does not satisfy the conditions for acquiring ownership or completing the transfer registration. Wang Guangzhi does not meet the circumstances set forth in Articles 25 to 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration by People's Courts that allow exclusion of execution. 3. If Wang Guangzhi's rights were infringed or the Apparel Store breached the contract, he should seek compensation from the tortfeasor or demand that the Apparel Store assume liability for breach of contract. In summary, Wang Guangzhi does not have rights and interests sufficient to preclude the court's preservation seizure of the property in dispute. The first-instance court found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and the judgment should be upheld.

He Fang argued in defense: It is true that Wang Guangzhi entered into a labor contract with the Apparel Store. After the Apparel Store was dissolved, Wang Guangzhi continued to perform the labor contract at other stores. The property in dispute is a welfare property that Wang Guangzhi should receive. If Wang Guangzhi had not completed the ten-year labor contract, the Apparel Store would not have given the property to Wang Guangzhi.

Wang Guangzhi's claims at first instance: 1. Confirm that Property A at Jiahong Road, Jinjiang District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province belongs to Wang Guangzhi; 2. Order He Fang to assist Wang Guangzhi in completing the procedures for the change of ownership registration of the property; 3. Order a stay of execution on Property A at Jiahong Road, Jinjiang District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, and lift the seizure measures; 4. Litigation costs shall be borne jointly by Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch and He Fang.

The first-instance court found the following facts: On December 2, 2008, Wang Guangzhi and the Apparel Store entered into a "Labor Contract" stipulating that the Apparel Store, for development needs, hired Wang Guangzhi as Department Manager. Main contents: Article 1: Type and term of contract: This contract is a fixed-term labor contract. The contract term is from January 1, 2009 to December 31, 2018; Article 2: Work content and place: The Apparel Store assigned Wang Guangzhi to work as Department Manager. The place of work was in Xiangtan City, Hunan Province; Article 4: Labor remuneration: Upon negotiation between the parties, Wang Guangzhi's wages were RMB 2,500 per month. On the same day, the parties also signed a "Supplementary Agreement to the Labor Contract," stipulating that the Apparel Store, for development needs, voluntarily provided Wang Guangzhi with a set of housing as a welfare benefit. Main contents: Article 1: The Apparel Store agreed that, under the condition that Wang Guangzhi signed a fixed-term labor contract for more than 10 years and actually performed it, the Apparel Store would provide Wang Guangzhi with a housing welfare benefit of a set of housing free of charge. This benefit was an additional, conditional special treatment provided by the Apparel Store to Wang Guangzhi, unrelated to Wang Guangzhi's labor remuneration and normal welfare benefits. Article 2: The Apparel Store was to purchase housing for Wang Guangzhi within the year 2009; the housing construction area was 110 square meters; the housing location: near the Third Ring Road, Chengdu; the payment method for the housing purchase was mortgage. Article 3: Housing payment method: 1. The housing property certificate and land use certificate were to be handled in the name of a person designated by the company, with the costs borne by the Apparel Store; 2. The down payment for the housing was to be paid 50% by the Apparel Store and 50% by Wang Guangzhi. When Wang Guangzhi completed a full 10 years of work at the Apparel Store, the Apparel Store would pay Wang Guangzhi the down payment he had expended in a lump sum; 3. Payment of housing mortgage installments: (1) The Apparel Store paid 50% each month, and Wang Guangzhi paid 50%; (2) Mortgage installments for the current year were to be paid in full by Wang Guangzhi first. In January of the following year, the Apparel Store would pay Wang Guangzhi in a lump sum the portion of the previous year's mortgage installments that the Apparel Store was obligated to pay. Future mortgage installment payments would follow this analogous payment method; (3) After the expiration of the contract term, when all housing mortgage installments were fully paid, the Apparel Store would settle with Wang Guangzhi in a lump sum the portion of mortgage installments borne by Wang Guangzhi within 30 days; 4. The welfare housing provided by the Apparel Store to Wang Guangzhi was a property with a construction area of 110 square meters. Treatment of the portion of the housing construction area exceeding the standard: The purchase price for the exceeding portion of the housing area was to be borne by Wang Guangzhi and paid to the Apparel Store in a lump sum. If the housing area was less than 110 square meters, the Apparel Store would only settle based on the actual area and would not compensate Wang Guangzhi for the difference. Article 4: Ownership agreement for the housing: 1. The housing property certificate, land use certificate, purchase invoice, and all other documents related to the housing were to be kept by the Apparel Store. After Wang Guangzhi fulfilled all obligations stipulated in the labor contract and supplementary agreement in accordance with the agreement, the Apparel Store would transfer the housing to Wang Guangzhi, and only then would Wang Guangzhi acquire ownership of the housing; 2. From the time of signing this contract and purchasing the housing, Wang Guangzhi had the right to use the housing. That is, Wang Guangzhi must work normally for more than ten years at his current job position (or an adjusted higher-level job position) before he could acquire ownership of the housing. Before the expiration of the contracted work period agreed upon, Wang Guangzhi only had the right to use the housing and the right to lease income, but did not have the right to dispose of it and could not transfer, mortgage, or donate it.

On June 13, 2009, Wang Guangzhi and He Fang, as purchasers, signed a "Commercial Housing Subscription Agreement" with Nanxin Company. Main contents: Wang Guangzhi and He Fang subscribed to Property B, Phase 1, Beverly International City, developed by Nanxin Company. The construction area was 129.48 square meters, unit price RMB 4,850 per square meter, total price RMB 602,082, and deposit RMB 30,000.

On June 13, 2009, Wang Guangzhi paid a deposit of RMB 30,000 using his personal bank card. The down payment for the property in dispute was RMB 292,082. The Apparel Store actually paid RMB 110,000, and Wang Guangzhi actually paid RMB 182,082. Thereafter, an account was opened in He Fang's name with the Agricultural Bank of China, and mortgage installments were paid monthly. Evidence presented by Wang Guangzhi showed that the sources of the mortgage installments in He Fang's said account were deposits made by Wang Guangzhi or his spouse Tang Lijia into He Fang's account starting from 2009. On July 31, 2017, Tang Lijia, Wang Guangzhi's spouse, repaid the remaining mortgage balance of RMB 246,161.83 in full through an internal deduction method from her bank account.

On October 9, 2010, the property in dispute was registered under the names of He Fang and her spouse Xian Jianzhang. On August 24, 2017, He Fang and her spouse divorced, agreeing that the property would belong to He Fang, and the change of registration was completed, with the property registered under He Fang's name alone. From October 2010 to January 2011, Wang Guangzhi renovated the property in dispute. Thereafter, he has resided there to the present.

The first-instance court also found: On August 2, 2017, Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch, in connection with a case of guarantee contract dispute with Chen Feiping, Zhou Donghai, Peng Congneng, He Fang, and Meishan Qisheng Building Materials Co., Ltd., applied for the seizure of the assets of Chen Feiping, Zhou Donghai, Peng Congneng, He Fang, and Meishan Qisheng Building Materials Co., Ltd. within a limit of RMB 110 million.

On August 23, 2017, the first-instance court issued a property preservation ruling in (2017) Sichuan Civil First Instance No. 85, seizing a total of 36 properties, including the property in dispute, within a limit of RMB 110 million. On February 5, 2018, Wang Guangzhi, as a third party, raised an objection to the execution of the preservation of the property in dispute, claiming that he was the actual owner of the property in dispute and requesting the lifting of the seizure on the property. On August 16, 2018, the first-instance court issued Civil Ruling (2017) Sichuan Civil First Instance No. 85 (3), dismissing Wang Guangzhi's objection. The ruling was served on Wang Guangzhi on August 30, 2018. On September 5, 2018, Wang Guangzhi filed the present lawsuit.

The business license of the Apparel Store as an individual industrial and commercial household showed that the operator's name was Ma Youzhong. Wang Guangzhi stated in the proceedings that the Apparel Store was dissolved at the end of 2014.

The first-instance court held that, based on the reasons for Wang Guangzhi's lawsuit and the defense of Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Cuqiao Sub-branch, the focal issue in this case was whether Wang Guangzhi had rights and interests in the property in dispute sufficient to preclude the court's preservation seizure in another case.

Pursuant to Article 27 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Property Preservation Cases by People's Courts, which states: "Where a people's court preserves property other than the subject matter of the litigation dispute, and a third party, dissatisfied with the preservation ruling or the enforcement actions during the implementation of the preservation ruling, raises a written objection based on substantive rights to the preserved property, the people's court shall review and handle it in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law and issue a ruling. If the third party or the preservation applicant is dissatisfied with that ruling, it may file a lawsuit of third-party objection to execution with the people's court within 15 days from the date of service of the ruling," since the first-instance court had already dismissed Wang Guangzhi's objection to the preservation ruling, Wang Guangzhi was entitled to file a third-party objection to execution lawsuit. The first-instance court's Civil Ruling (2017) Sichuan Civil First Instance No. 85 (3) dismissing Wang Guangzhi's objection was served on Wang Guangzhi on August 30, 2018. Wang Guangzhi submitted his complaint on September 5, 2018, so his lawsuit met the procedural requirements prescribed by law.

Furthermore, according to Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides: "In a lawsuit of third-party objection to execution or a lawsuit of execution applicant's objection, the third party shall bear the burden of proof that it has civil rights and interests sufficient to preclude compulsory enforcement over the subject matter of execution," and Article 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration by People's Courts, which provides: "In the enforcement of monetary claims, where a buyer raises an objection to real estate registered under the name of the person subject to enforcement, and the following circumstances are met and the buyer's rights can exclude execution, the people's court shall support the objection: (1) a lawful and effective written sales contract was signed before the court's seizure; (2) the real estate has been lawfully possessed before the court's seizure; (3) the full purchase price has been paid, or part of the purchase price has been paid as agreed and the remaining price is delivered to the court for enforcement as required by the court; (4) the failure to complete the transfer registration was not due to the buyer's own reasons," only when Wang Guangzhi proves that his rights to the property in dispute simultaneously satisfy all four of the above conditions can it possibly produce the effect of precluding court enforcement.

The first-instance court held that Wang Guangzhi did not satisfy the requirements of items (1) and (4) of the aforementioned judicial interpretation, and thus did not have civil rights and interests sufficient to preclude execution over the property in dispute. The reasons are as follows:

First, no real estate sale relationship was formed between Wang Guangzhi and He Fang. Based on the evidence presented by Wang Guangzhi, his rights to possess, use, and derive income from the property in dispute were established on the basis of the labor relationship formed with the Apparel Store actually operated by He Fang. It was a welfare property provided by the Apparel Store, and only upon Wang Guangzhi fulfilling the condition of serving the Apparel Store for 10 years could the property be transferred to Wang Guangzhi. However, the contract stipulated that the time for Wang Guangzhi to acquire ownership of the property in dispute was the date of expiration of the labor contract between Wang Guangzhi and the Apparel Store, i.e., December 31, 2018. According to the above agreement, the condition for acquiring the property had not been fulfilled.

Second, Wang Guangzhi claimed that the Apparel Store was dissolved in 2014, but after the dissolution, he did not negotiate with He Fang regarding the ownership or transfer of the property in dispute. Furthermore, after Wang Guangzhi fully paid off all mortgage installments on the property in July 2017 through his spouse Tang Lijia's account, He Fang transferred the property into her own name due to divorce in August 2017, and Wang Guangzhi raised no objection to this. Therefore, it should be determined that Wang Guangzhi himself was at fault for the ultimate failure to complete the transfer registration.

Regarding Wang Guangzhi's claim for confirmation that he is the owner of the property in dispute and for an order that He Fang assist in the transfer registration, the first-instance court held that, as previously stated, since the conditions for the transfer of ownership of the property in dispute as stipulated in the Labor Contract had not been fulfilled, and there was no evidence that He Fang and Wang Guangzhi negotiated and reached a consensus on the transfer of the property, the property in dispute, registered under He Fang's name, should be determined to belong to He Fang. Accordingly, this claim of Wang Guangzhi was also untenable and was not supported.

In summary, Wang Guangzhi's claims could not be established. The first-instance court, in accordance with Article 64 and Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 28 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Execution Objections and Reconsideration by People's Courts, ruled: Dismiss Wang Guangzhi's claims. The first-instance acceptance fee was RMB 10,700, to be borne by Wang Guangzhi.

During the second instance in this Court, the parties submitted evidence in support of their appellate claims in accordance with the law. This Court organized the parties to exchange evidence and conduct cross-examination.

Wang Guangzhi submitted the following evidence: 1. Bank statement of Wang Guangzhi's China Construction Bank card, intended to prove that the mortgage installments for the property were paid by Wang Guangzhi. 2. Real estate sales contract between Wang Guangzhi and Ye Hongxiang and transfer vouchers, intended to prove that the balance of over RMB 200,000 for the property was paid by Wang Guangzhi. 3. Wang Guangzhi's salary records, intended to prove the existence of a genuine labor relationship between Wang Guangzhi and the Apparel Store. 4. Personal housing information of Wang Guangzhi and his spouse, intended to prove that Wang Guangzhi and his spouse have another property in Jinjiang District, Chengdu, but without property registration, and that they currently have no house. 5. Household registration booklets of Wang Guangzhi and his daughter, intended to prove that because his daughter was attending primary school, he discussed with He Fang about transferring the property to Wang Guangzhi's name ahead of schedule. 6. Copies of 15 documents from 2013 to 2018, including Wang Guangzhi's appointment letters, meeting minutes, safety target responsibility letters, decoration and renovation project contracts, etc., and a statement from Sichuan Sanyangkai Tai Enterprise Management Consulting Co., Ltd. confirming that the copies were made from originals held by that company, intended to prove that after the dissolution of the Apparel Store in 2014, Wang Guangzhi continued to perform management duties at other chain stores as required by the company's investors.

Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank, Cuqiao Sub-branch challenged the authenticity of Evidence 2, but had no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 1, 3, 4, and 5, although it believed that they could not achieve Wang Guangzhi's purpose of proof. As for Evidence 6, it argued that 14 of the documents were formed before the first-instance trial and did not constitute new evidence, and that these pieces of evidence lacked relevance to the facts to be proved.

In response, this Court holds that the Cuqiao Sub-branch has no objection to the authenticity of Evidence 1, 3, 4, and 5, and this Court confirms their authenticity. Evidence 6 can reflect the relationship among the chain stores of "Sanyang Kaitai" and also Wang Guangzhi's positions in the corresponding stores, and this Court accepts it as evidence. Evidence 2 is intended to prove that Wang Guangzhi paid over RMB 200,000 of the remaining mortgage balance, a fact already determined by the first-instance court. This evidence is irrelevant to the facts to be proved and its authenticity is in doubt, so this Court does not admit it. As for whether the other evidence can prove that Wang Guangzhi has civil rights and interests in the property in question sufficient to exclude enforcement, this Court will determine that in light of all evidence in the case.

The following facts are found by this Court at second instance:

On December 2, 2008, the Clothing Store (Party A) and Wang Guangzhi (Party B) entered into a Supplemental Agreement to the Labor Contract, Article 11 of which stipulated: If Party A is forced to cease operations due to various unexpected circumstances and the company is dissolved, this contract shall continue to be performed (i.e., any shareholder has the right to require Party B to continue to perform the contract until its expiration).

On July 26, 2009, the Clothing Store (Party A) and Wang Guangzhi (Party B) executed a Statement, stating: Within six months after the expiration of the "contract," Party A shall transfer the property to Party B's name. Party A shall pay the down payment of RMB 110,000, and Party B shall pay RMB 130,000. The mortgage shall be repaid within 10 years. Each year, when Party A pays Party B 50% of the mortgage payment as agreed in the "contract," Party B shall issue a receipt to Party A. The receipt must be signed by both Party A and Party B, with Party A's representative being Chen Feiping or He Fang, and Party B being Wang Guangzhi himself.

On January 28, 2018, Chen Feiping, representative of the Clothing Store, issued a Statement of Facts, stating: The Clothing Store was dissolved in 2014. The labor period involved in the labor contract signed between Wang Guangzhi and the store had approached ten years. The apartment located in Beverly International City, which the store gave to Wang Guangzhi, now belongs to Wang Guangzhi. Wang Guangzhi himself paid all mortgage payments, and the portion contributed by the company was a welfare reward from the company for Wang Guangzhi's work.

During the second-instance trial, Wang Guangzhi stated that the "Room B, Phase 1, Beverly International City" indicated in the Commercial Housing Subscription Agreement dated June 13, 2009 is the room located at No. A, Jiahong Road, Jinjiang District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province, which was later sealed by the court.

This Court confirms the other facts found by the first-instance court.

Opinion of the Court

Based on the parties' appeal requests, reply opinions, and relevant evidence, and confirmed by the parties in court, the issues in dispute at second instance are: 1. Whether Wang Guangzhi has ownership of the property in question; 2. Whether Wang Guangzhi has civil rights and interests in the property in question sufficient to exclude the preservative seizure. The analysis is as follows:

1. Regarding whether Wang Guangzhi has ownership of the property in question

Article 9 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "The creation, alteration, transfer, or extinction of a real right in immovable property shall become effective upon registration in accordance with the law; without registration, it shall not become effective, unless otherwise provided by law." That is to say, for a change in real right in immovable property based on a juridical act, in addition to requiring a lawful and valid juridical act, completion of registration in the immovable property register is also a condition for the change to take effect. In this case, the property in question is immovable property, so the transfer of ownership must be registered in accordance with the law, and the effect of a change in ownership occurs only after registration is completed. Although the property was purchased by Wang Guangzhi and He Fang as buyers from Nanxin Company under a Commercial Housing Subscription Agreement signed on June 13, 2009, the ownership of the property is currently registered only in He Fang's name. Therefore, Wang Guangzhi's claim of ownership over the property has no factual or legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

2. Regarding whether Wang Guangzhi has civil rights and interests in the property in question sufficient to exclude the preservative seizure

This Court holds that Article 311 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where an outsider to the action or the applying party for enforcement initiates a lawsuit on objection to enforcement, the outsider shall bear the burden of proof to show that he has civil rights and interests in the subject matter of enforcement sufficient to exclude enforcement." Therefore, the purpose of the system of lawsuits on objection to enforcement by outsiders is to resolve the issue of whether an outsider has the right to exclude enforcement of the subject matter of enforcement.

The assessment of this issue should be based on the provisions of laws and judicial interpretations regarding civil rights (interests). The current laws and judicial interpretations provide relatively general rules on lawsuits on objection to enforcement by outsiders. In particular, the types, scope, and conditions of "civil rights and interests sufficient to exclude enforcement" as provided by laws and judicial interpretations are not clearly stipulated not only in laws but also in relevant judicial interpretations applicable to civil procedure. Only certain judicial interpretations applicable to enforcement procedures, such as the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Seizure, Impoundment, and Freezing of Property in Civil Enforcement by People's Courts and the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Handling of Objections and Reconsideration Cases in Enforcement by People's Courts, provide incomplete lists and provisions. Therefore, in the current trial of cases involving lawsuits on objection to enforcement by outsiders, whether the civil rights and interests claimed by the outsider over the subject matter of enforcement are sufficient to exclude enforcement may be examined with reference to the relevant provisions of the above-mentioned judicial interpretations applicable to enforcement procedures. However, at the same time, one should not be completely bound by the provisions of these judicial interpretations applicable to enforcement procedures. Even if the civil rights and interests enjoyed by an outsider are not within the situations provided for in the above judicial interpretations, it does not necessarily mean that they cannot exclude enforcement. Whether the outsider's claim to exclude enforcement can be established should be determined by, on the basis of identifying the substantive law nature and effect of the relevant parties' civil rights (interests) over the subject matter of enforcement according to the provisions of laws and judicial interpretations on civil rights (interests), through exploration and analysis of the hierarchical relationship between relevant legal norms, the values behind them, and the legislative purposes, and in combination with the specific circumstances of different cases, such as the identity and occupational characteristics of the relevant parties, the degree of fault regarding the defective title status of the subject matter of enforcement, the exercise of rights related to the transaction of the subject matter of enforcement, the performance of the transaction, and even further exploration of the impact of the subject matter of enforcement on the basic living security and pursuit of order of the relevant parties.

In this case, first, regarding the source of the rights of the relevant parties over the property: Wang Guangzhi and the Clothing Store had a labor relationship. According to the Supplemental Agreement to the Labor Contract, during the performance of the Labor Contract, Wang Guangzhi had the right to possess, use, and profit from the property, and with the continuous performance of the Labor Contract, Wang Guangzhi would ultimately obtain ownership of the property after the expiration of the contract period. He Fang, as the nominal registered owner, had the sole purpose of binding Wang Guangzhi to fulfill the ten-year labor obligations under the Labor Contract, and actually had no other rights over the property. After the contract period expired, Wang Guangzhi had the right to request He Fang to assist in the transfer registration of the property. In this case, although the Clothing Store was dissolved in 2014, according to the contract, Wang Guangzhi was still obligated after the dissolution to continue to perform the contract until its expiration as required by the shareholders of the Clothing Store, and Wang Guangzhi actually continued to work at other chain clothing stores until the ten-year labor contract expired. Chen Feiping, one of the actual operators of the Clothing Store, also issued a Statement of Facts indicating that the labor period involved in the labor contract signed between the Clothing Store and Wang Guangzhi had approached ten years, Wang Guangzhi paid all remaining mortgage payments, and the property in question was actually owned by Wang Guangzhi. In contrast, the Cuqiao Sub-branch did not present evidence that Wang Guangzhi failed to perform the ten-year labor contract as agreed and could not obtain the property as agreed. Therefore, after Wang Guangzhi fully performed the ten-year labor contract, he has corresponding rights over the property. On the other hand, the relationship between the Cuqiao Sub-branch and He Fang is one of a suretyship contract. The former's rights over the property stem from the enforcement procedure, with the underlying basis being its creditor's rights as a commercial entity against He Fang arising from He Fang's obligation to perform the suretyship. Moreover, there is no evidence that these creditor's rights were formed based on reliance on the registered title status of the property.

Second, regarding the nature of the relevant parties' rights over the property: Although the Supplemental Agreement to the Labor Contract explicitly states that the property is unrelated to Wang Guangzhi's labor remuneration and normal welfare benefits, it also clearly states that the property provided by the Clothing Store is "as a welfare benefit" and describes this benefit as "an additional, conditional special treatment provided by the Clothing Store to Wang Guangzhi." From the parties' agreement and the performance of the labor contract, the property would become Wang Guangzhi's ownership due to his fulfillment of the obligations under the labor contract. Therefore, it clearly contains certain elements of labor consideration. To some extent, Wang Guangzhi's rights over the property actually embody a considerable portion of his labor付出 for working for the employer for ten years and should fall within the scope of labor remuneration in a broad sense. Moreover, the vast majority of the purchase price for the property has been actually paid by Wang Guangzhi, and Wang Guangzhi finished decorating and moved in in 2011 and has lived there ever since. Under these circumstances, in the enforcement procedure targeting the property in this case, granting priority protection to Wang Guangzhi's rights over the property, compared with the Cuqiao Sub-branch's surety creditor's rights based on He Fang's obligation to perform the suretyship, conforms to the basic spirit of the law in protecting the laborer's right to obtain labor remuneration and is therefore quite legitimate and reasonable.

Third, regarding the transaction model for the property: The Labor Contract stipulates that the property is a welfare apartment allocated by the Clothing Store to Wang Guangzhi. During the term of the labor contract, the property is registered in He Fang's name. After the contract expires, it can be transferred to Wang Guangzhi's name. From the date of purchase and delivery, the property is occupied and used by Wang Guangzhi. Although this transaction model bears some similarity to a nominal purchase, it is different from a nominal purchase in the general sense. The property was temporarily registered in the name of a person designated by the Clothing Store to prevent Wang Guangzhi from leaving early. Wang Guangzhi passively accepted the arrangement for the registration of ownership of the property due to his disadvantaged position in the labor contract, which is not a completely equal civil legal relationship. He did not actively seek to obtain improper benefits through such means, nor did he harm national interests or social public interests. Therefore, this transactional arrangement among the relevant parties is not illegal or improper, and thus Wang Guangzhi is not legally blameworthy for it. Furthermore, the Labor Contract was signed in December 2008, far earlier than the formation of the creditor's rights of the preservative seizure applicant and the time of the court's seizure. Therefore, there is no evidence that Wang Guangzhi, as an outsider, and He Fang, as the execution debtor, engaged in conduct to evade debts or avoid enforcement through the transactional arrangement for the property.

Finally, regarding the reason why the ownership transfer for the property was not completed: After the Clothing Store was dissolved in 2014, to expedite the transfer of ownership of the property, Wang Guangzhi negotiated with the Clothing Store and repaid the remaining mortgage in a lump sum before the expiration of the labor contract. This should be regarded as Wang Guangzhi actively exercising his rights. About one month after paying off the mortgage, the property was seized by the court. However, considering the time stipulation in the Statement that "within six months after the expiration of the 'contract,' Party A shall transfer the property to Party B's name," and the fact that Wang Guangzhi repaid the remaining mortgage early, it can be comprehensively determined that the failure to transfer the property to Wang Guangzhi's name before the court's seizure was not due to his reasons.

In summary, the property in question is part of the labor remuneration that Wang Guangzhi should obtain for performing the labor contract. Now that he has performed the corresponding obligations under the labor contract, compared with the Cuqiao Sub-branch's surety creditor's rights based on He Fang's obligation to perform the suretyship, Wang Guangzhi's reasonable expectation of rights over the property should be protected. Therefore, his request to exclude the preservative seizure of the property under the property preservation ruling of (2017) Chuan Min Chu No. 85 is supported by this Court.

Additionally, regarding Wang Guangzhi's request for He Fang to assist in the transfer of ownership registration of the property, this Court holds that according to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China concerning lawsuits on objection to enforcement, such lawsuits are intended to resolve conflicts among relevant parties' civil rights and interests in enforcement proceedings. Except where, according to laws and judicial interpretations, an outsider's claim for confirmation of rights may be heard and adjudicated together in a lawsuit on objection to enforcement because it is closely related to the determination of civil rights and interests, claims raised by the outsider in such lawsuits that require the execution debtor to continue performing the contract, assist in the transfer registration, deliver the subject matter, or pay liquidated damages, etc., are not within the scope of trial of lawsuits on objection to enforcement, as they are unrelated to the purpose of excluding enforcement, and are also inappropriate for consolidated hearing. Therefore, Wang Guangzhi's request for He Fang to assist in the transfer registration of the property is not within the scope of trial in this case.

In conclusion, Wang Guangzhi's appeal is partially sustained. In accordance with Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 312 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The civil judgment (2018) Chuan Min Chu No. 112 of the Sichuan High People's Court is reversed;

2. The property located at No. A, Jiahong Road, Jinjiang District, Chengdu, Sichuan Province shall not be sealed;

3. Wang Guangzhi's other claims are dismissed.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 10,700, and the court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 10,700, both to be borne by Chengdu Rural Commercial Bank Co., Ltd., Cuqiao Sub-branch.

This judgment is final.
